issue_context.title: Typing default value of column and protect type for a function
issue_context.body:
### Issue description

Typing default value of column and protect type for a function

### Expected Behavior

The `default` parameter in `Column` should be typed

### Actual Behavior

The `default` parameter in `Column` is an `any` type. It made me fall on a incomprehensible error: 
```TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'toUpperCase')```
This error appears when the function returns a type different from string

### Steps to reproduce

``` typescript

@Entity("test")
export class test {
    @Column({ name: "test_column", default: () => null })
    test_column: string
}

```

### My Environment

| Dependency          | Version  |
| ---                 | ---      |
| Operating System    |          |
| Node.js version     | v16.17.1  |
| Typescript version  | 4.9.3  |
| TypeORM version     | 0.3.11  |


### Additional Context

_No response_

review_comments: I'm not sure if it won't be a breaking change. I'm not sure what value users could use in this place (Date? Buffer? Anything else that was just stringified and was working?).
callback definition is invalid. Should be `() => Promise.all()`
how it can be instance of `Date` if it is defined as `date: number` in Entity?
we should not test only oracle.

column type should be `timestamp`
`Date.now` should be truncated to fit javascript `number` size -> `Math.round(Date.now() / 1000)`
